assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Neuland Laboratories (consolidated, Rs crore; no minorities, so Screener's Net Profit is attributable profit and no patch is needed). Neuland reports one audited segment; its decks split revenue into CMS (CDMO), Prime APIs, Specialty APIs and Others. The engine runs one revenue-growth path and the four-line build sits in businessLines, checked against model revenue in tools/authoring/NEULANDLAB.ctx.js. EBITDA is on Screener's basis (before other income; the company's 'EBITDA' includes other income). Other income and interest are built in NEULANDLAB.ctx.js and entered here (treasuryYield 0). Valued on P/E, the method of most brokers that disclose one.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the four-line build below (checked in NEULANDLAB.ctx.js). FY27 +20%: management 'aspired to grow at about 20%, and we expect that FY27 & FY28 also' (Q1FY27 call), CRISIL expects >15%; Q1FY27 revenue Rs642 cr (+119%) already covers 26% of our FY27, and Q2-Q4 need only ~Rs1,790 cr vs Rs1,730 cr a year earlier, because Q4FY26 was 'a Q3 plus Q4' quarter. FY28 +16% / FY29 +15%: below the 18-20% aspiration, which management itself calls 'aspirational' and 'not linear'; peptides add revenue only from FY28 (CRISIL). Street (Nuvama, Dec-2025): FY27E Rs2,598 cr, FY28E Rs2,818 cr; Goldman (May-2026): 20%+ revenue CAGR FY26-28E.

base._why: FY26 revenue Rs2,023.0 cr: CMS Rs1,244 cr (commercial Rs1,146 cr + development Rs98 cr, Q4FY26 deck); Prime 23% and Specialty 11% of revenue (FY26 deck; CRISIL: Prime -5%, Specialty -16%); Others = residual (4.5%; the deck rounds Others to 6%).

businessLines._why: CMS +27% in FY27: Q1FY27 CMS Rs438 cr vs Rs133 cr a year earlier; 'about 3' commercial molecules drive it with 'a fairly healthy future over the next 5 to 6 years'; one more commercialisation in FY27 and development revenue rising; we assume Q2-Q4 CMS of ~Rs1,140 cr vs Rs1,111 cr a year earlier (the inflated Q4FY26 makes the comparison hard). +20% in FY28 (one or two commercialisations, first peptide revenue) and +18% in FY29. Prime +10/8/7%: Q1FY27 Prime ~Rs116 cr (+23%), Ezetimibe 'likely to drive growth'; FY26 fell 5%. Specialty +8/12/12%: FY26 fell 16% on Paliperidone shipment delays at a customer; Q1FY27 ~Rs51 cr (+10%); Gland Pharma sterile collaboration and new DMFs (Vonoprazan, Edoxaban) later. Others grow with the business.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (before other income): 15.1% (FY22), 22.9% (FY23), 29.7% (FY24), 22.4% (FY25), 28.7% (FY26), 34.7% in Q1FY27 (Q4FY26 39.6%, Q1FY26 11.6%). Margins follow revenue (operating leverage on ~45% fixed costs: employees 17%, manufacturing and other costs ~17-18% of sales) and the CMS share (61% in FY26, 67% in Q1FY27). FY27 31%: Q2-Q4 at ~29.7% vs 31.6% a year earlier. FY28-29 30.5%: the peptide plant and the new R&D centre add fixed costs before revenue, and FY26 had 'favourable conditions in terms of exchange rates'. Management's own planning margin is '25% plus'; Nuvama (Dec-2025) 32%/32% for FY27-28E.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 Rs397 cr; Q1FY27 Rs122 cr. Rs1,460 cr approved over 13 quarters with Rs870 cr spent leaves ~Rs590 cr committed (peptide Phase II by end-FY27, the ~Rs190 cr R&D centre, the Rs196 cr Unit 1 expansion). FY27 Rs480 cr = Q1 Rs122 cr + ~Rs360 cr of committed projects; FY28-29 Rs450 cr a year: the rest of the committed list plus land and new blocks ('forward capex will be much higher than the capex that we've deployed so far'; CRISIL rates Rs522 cr of proposed term loans).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs91.7 cr (incl. right-of-use assets); Q1FY27 Rs27 cr (Rs108 cr annualised) as the R&D centre lease and Unit 3 block started. The engine depreciates capex from the year it is spent but holds CWIP (Rs211 cr at Mar-26) flat; 6.8% on gross block plus capex gives ~Rs120 / 152 / 183 cr for FY27-29E, in line with the new peptide plant, R&D centre and blocks being commissioned.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Treasury income is built in tools/authoring/NEULANDLAB.ctx.js on AVERAGE gross cash (engine net cash plus our borrowing path) and entered in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (checked in NEULANDLAB.ctx.js; written by NEULANDLAB.mult.js): (1) treasury income at 5% on average gross cash and deposits = engine net cash (Rs56 / 18 / 94 / 262 cr, Mar-26 to Mar-29E, after leases) plus our borrowing path (debt Rs197 / 300 / 350 / 350 cr, leases Rs105 / 100 / 95 / 90 cr); FY26 earned 4.9% (interest on deposits Rs10.1 cr plus mutual-fund gains Rs7.6 cr on average cash, deposits and funds of ~Rs361 cr); (2) write-backs of Rs1.5 cr (FY25 Rs1.6 cr, FY26 Rs2.0 cr). No forex gains are forecast (FY26 Rs10.6 cr, helped by the weak rupee). FY26 other income Rs30.2 cr (company) / Rs24.9 cr (Screener, net of a Rs5.3 cr loss on asset sales); twelve months to Jun-26 Rs30.0 cr (Screener).
assumptions._interestWhy: Built in NEULANDLAB.ctx.js: 7.5% on average bank debt (Rs197 → 300 → 350 → 350 cr; CRISIL: capex partly debt-funded, Rs130 cr R&D-centre loan tied up, Rs522 cr of proposed term loans rated) + 7.5% on average lease liabilities (Rs105 → 100 → 95 → 90 cr; the R&D-centre lease) + Rs5 cr of other borrowing costs net of capitalisation. FY26 finance cost Rs23.9 cr (borrowings Rs11.7 cr, leases Rs7.0 cr, other Rs6.8 cr, capitalised -Rs1.5 cr); Q1FY27 Rs7 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 25.6% (Rs125.0 cr on Rs489.0 cr), Q1FY27 25.4%; statutory 25.17% plus non-deductible items (CSR) and foreign subsidiaries.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs34 a share = 12.0% payout (FY25 Rs12, 5.9%; FY24 Rs14, 6.0%). We keep 12% while capex is heavy.

dcf._betaWhy: Neuland has net cash, so WACC equals the cost of equity. Beta 1.0 (12.5%): three customer groups are 54% of revenue, a handful of CMS molecules drive profit, and quarters swing from 12% to 40% margins. The company tests goodwill at a 12.5% post-tax discount rate (AR FY26 note 37).
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5%, mid-range of the house 5-6%; the company's own goodwill test uses 5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~15% (FY29E) to 7% by FY42E: revenue grew 15% a year in FY16-26 with long flat spells (FY18, FY22, FY25).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 26% by FY42E, below our FY29E 30.5% and near management's '25% plus': today's commercial CMS molecules lose patent protection over the next decade and generic API pricing is tough.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from 14-20% of sales (FY27-29E) to 7%: maintenance (~4.5% of sales, FY26 depreciation) plus growth capex at ~2.5x asset turnover.
dcf._wcNote: Operating working capital on Screener's Mar-26 balance sheet is ~37% of FY26 sales (137 days, a peak; 84 days at Jun-26). The engine holds the ratio, so our cash path is conservative if working capital normalises.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The commercial CMS molecules keep growing with their brands, one or two new molecules and the first peptide programmes commercialise on time, and Specialty recovers; growth runs ~5 points a year faster and the margin ~2 points higher.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: A big CMS customer destocks or second-sources (a takeover, a weak launch), as in FY25 when revenue fell 5%; peptides slip a year and GDS pricing stays tough; growth ~8 points a year slower and the margin ~4 points lower, near FY25's 22%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Neuland: of the brokers whose method we could see, Nuvama uses P/E (48x H1FY28E EPS, Dec-2025), Goldman Sachs a sum of the parts on P/E (its CRO/CDMO framework) and B&K P/E (38x FY27E, 2024); one broker reported in Aug-2026 uses 30x Jun-28E EV/EBITDA. 28.5x = Neuland's median one-year-forward P/E since 1-Apr-2021 (every weekly close plus the 30-Sep close, 288 points; forward EPS = the next full fiscal year's realised EPS, FY25 before the Rs76.4 cr gain on the Nanakramguda property (Rs148.8 vs Rs202.7 reported; the median is 24.1x on reported EPS), our FY27E/FY28E) of 26.4x x 1.082 (the nine pharma peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians, PLAYBOOK §7c, Neuland outside the set; reproduced +8.2%) = 28.6x, nearest half-turn. Trough rule: no year is left out (FY23 Rs127.5 vs a Rs31.4 line, half of FY21's Rs62.9; FY25 Rs148.8 vs Rs116.9). Earnings stepped up from FY23 but not from a loss, so the turnaround rule does not apply: the window from the break (1-Apr-2022) x the peers' same-window move gives 37x, a sensitivity row. Bull 45x / bear 13.5x = 75th / 25th percentile (41.4x / 12.7x) x 1.082. No own-move blend, no growth uplift (sensitivities only). Written by NEULANDLAB.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check: Neuland's median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since 1-Apr-2021 (EV at each weekly close = price x 1.283 cr shares less the last published company net cash, over the next full year's EBITDA, Screener basis) of 15.9x x 1.075 (the nine peers' five-year EV/EBITDA move; reproduced +7.5%) = 17.1x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EBITDA plus Sep-28E net cash. Bull 27x / bear 9x = 75th / 25th percentile x 1.075.

methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 12.5% (cost of equity = WACC; net cash), terminal growth 5.5%, plus net cash at Mar-27.

cover.headline: A few innovator molecules doubled Neuland's contract-manufacturing business; the market pays ~49x Sep-28E EPS for it, our rule gives 28.5x: target {{dcf.tp|inr}}, SELL
cover.lead: Neuland Laboratories makes active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) in Hyderabad: generic APIs for drug makers (Prime and Specialty, 34% of FY26 revenue) and, under exclusive contracts, APIs for innovators' new drugs (Custom Manufacturing Solutions, CMS, 61%). FY26 revenue rose 37% to ₹2,023 cr and EPS to ₹284 as CMS nearly doubled to ₹1,244 cr; Q1FY27 revenue rose 119%. "About 3" commercial molecules drive CMS, and three customer groups were 54% of FY26 revenue. We forecast EPS of ₹361.7 / 405.3 / 465.3 for FY27-29E. Most brokers that disclose a method use **P/E**, and so do we: Neuland's median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (26.4x, FY25 before a property gain), lifted 8.2% for the pharma sector's re-rating, gives **28.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹435.7 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL**. Starting the window at the FY23 earnings break gives 37x (₹16,120), still a SELL. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹12,411; DCF ₹6,145. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

sections.title: A Hyderabad API maker with two businesses: generic APIs sold to many, and contract-made APIs for a few innovators, which now bring 61% of revenue

blocks.p: Neuland makes **active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs)**: the chemical in a medicine that does the work. It does not make tablets, so it does not compete with its customers. It has two businesses. (1) **Generic Drug Substances (GDS)** sells off-patent APIs to generic drug makers in 80+ countries: **Prime APIs** are ~12 large-volume, mature molecules such as mirtazapine (an antidepressant), ezetimibe (cholesterol) and escitalopram, where price competition is tough; **Specialty APIs** are 50+ complex, low-volume molecules such as apixaban (a blood thinner), sterile paliperidone and aripiprazole injectables, and donepezil, with fewer competitors. (2) **Custom Manufacturing Solutions (CMS)** develops and makes APIs and intermediates for innovators' new drugs under exclusive contracts, from pre-clinical batches to commercial supply. Neuland has 1,226 kL of reactors in three plants near Hyderabad, 2,272 employees (406 in R&D) and 1,010+ regulatory filings.

sections.title: Forty years from a single API to a CDMO: an early bet on Unit III that cost five lean years, a promoter merger, a property sale and a leadership split

blocks.p: Dr. Davuluri Rama Mohan Rao founded Neuland in 1984; it sold its first API (salbutamol) in 1986, listed in 1994 and was among the first Indian API makers audited by the USFDA (1997). It opened offices in the US (2004) and Japan (2007) to build the CMS business that his son Saharsh Rao has run for ~19 years. In FY18 it bought Unit III and merged in two promoter-linked companies (Neuland Health Sciences, which held peptide R&D and Neuland shares, and Neuland Pharma Research), creating ₹279 cr of goodwill. Unit III sat largely idle until FY21. Since FY23 CMS commercial molecules have transformed earnings. In FY25 Neuland transferred a property in Hyderabad (₹76.4 cr gain); from 1-Apr-2026 Saharsh Rao became CEO & MD and his brother Sucheth Rao Executive Vice Chairman.

sections.title: Industry: a ~USD260 bn global CDMO market growing 6-7% a year, India's share rising as innovators diversify away from China; peptides the fastest-growing niche

blocks.p: Drug companies increasingly outsource the making of their APIs. The global pharmaceutical CDMO market was ~USD258.9 bn in 2025 and is forecast at ~USD374.7 bn by 2031 (~6-7% a year); India's CDMO market, ~USD25.8 bn in 2025, is forecast to roughly double to ~USD57.9 bn by 2031 (company MD&A, citing industry sources). Two forces help Indian suppliers: biotechs, which rarely own plants, now originate 76% of new small-molecule approvals (60% in 2016), and US policy (the Section 232 investigation, tariff threats) has pushed innovators to add non-Chinese sources. Peptide APIs, driven by GLP-1 drugs, are the fastest-growing niche: ~USD6 bn in 2025 to ~USD14 bn by 2030. The generic API market is larger but slower (~USD326.5 bn globally, ~4.8% a year to 2035) and fiercely price-competitive.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the tailwind is real but narrow. It reaches Neuland through a handful of CMS molecules (61% of FY26 revenue) rather than through the whole business, which is why growth is fast but lumpy.

sections.title: CMS: ₹282 cr to ₹1,244 cr in four years on commercial molecules; about three molecules and five customers carry it, and the quarters are lumpy

blocks.p: CMS earns money in two ways. **Development** revenue comes from process research and from batches for clinical trials and launches (₹98 cr in FY26, down from ₹303 cr in FY24, when launch quantities were large). **Commercial** revenue comes from supplying the API of an approved drug for as long as the innovator orders it (₹1,146 cr in FY26, from ₹114 cr in FY22). Neuland is usually written into the innovator's regulatory filing, which makes it hard to replace, but it also means its revenue rises and falls with a few drugs. The CEO is candid: "CMS commercial is being driven by a handful of molecules... maybe about 3 of them that really drive our business", with "a fairly healthy future for them over the next 5 to 6 years", but "there will be lumpiness". Neuland does not name them. Brokers and analysts link its commercial supplies to **xanomeline** (in BMS's schizophrenia drug Cobenfy, approved in the US in Sep-2024), **bempedoic acid** (Esperion's cholesterol drug; Daiichi Sankyo in Europe) and **deutetrabenazine** (Teva's Austedo) (B&K, Oct-2024; Q4FY26 call). Esperion received a takeover bid in May-2026; management says supply agreements usually survive a change of owner.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: real in complex chemistry, regulatory record and CMS lock-in; weak in generic pricing and diversification; unproven in peptides

blocks.p: A moat is a lasting advantage that lets a company earn more than its cost of capital for longer than rivals. Neuland has three genuine ones. First, chemistry: four decades of difficult reactions (deuterated molecules, chiral and cryogenic chemistry, peptide fragments) let it win development work that turns into exclusive supply. Second, a clean regulatory record over three USFDA-inspected plants, which innovators value above price. Third, lock-in: once its API is in an approved drug's filing, switching takes years. Its weaknesses are just as clear: generic Prime APIs are a price game, and in CMS the business rests on a few molecules owned by a few customers. Peptides are a bet, not yet an advantage.

sections.title: Valuation: 28.5x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the price pays ~49x and needs ~26% growth for 15 years

blocks.p: Of the four broker notes whose method we could see, three rest on **P/E** (Nuvama 48x H1FY28E; Goldman Sachs a sum of the parts on P/E; B&K 38x FY27E, an older note) and one on **EV/EBITDA** (30x Jun-28E, a broker reported in Aug-2026). We therefore value on **P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E)**, with EV/EBITDA and a DCF as cross-checks. Neuland has no minorities and our forecasts carry no exceptional items, so forecast EPS needs no adjustment.

We use Neuland's one-year-forward P/E **since 1-Apr-2021** (PLAYBOOK §4) on every weekly close plus the 30-Sep-2026 close (288 points): price ÷ the next full fiscal year's EPS as it actually turned out. Forward EPS is FY23 for dates in FY22, FY24 for FY23, FY25 for FY24, FY26 for FY25, our FY27E for FY26 and our FY28E for Apr-Sep 2026. **Exceptional item:** FY25 included a ₹76.4 cr gain on transferring the Nanakramguda property (~₹69 cr after tax by our estimate, a quarter of FY25 profit), so the base uses FY25 EPS before it (₹148.8 vs ₹202.74 reported; batch practice A18). The reported-EPS median is 24.1x (sensitivity). **Trough rule:** no year is left out: FY23 EPS (₹127.45) is far above half the prior three-year peak (₹31.4, half of FY21's ₹62.9), and FY25 before the gain (₹148.8) is above half of FY24's ₹233.9 (₹116.9). We multiply the median by the nine pharma peers' five-year move (+8.2%; Neuland is outside the set) and round to the nearest half-turn. No blend with Neuland's own move, no growth uplift (sensitivities below).

blocks.h: The earnings step-up: does it change the window?

blocks.p: Neuland's EPS stepped up sharply from FY23 (₹49.7 in FY22, ₹127.5 in FY23, ₹233.9 in FY24), but not from a loss or near-zero EPS, so the batch turnaround rule (PLAYBOOK §7c) does not apply and we follow §4 as written: the window runs from Apr-2021. That choice matters a lot here. Because the forward P/E uses EPS as it actually came in, the market's failure to foresee the jumps shows up as very low multiples: in FY23 the stock traded at 4.4-7.7x the FY24 EPS that followed, and in FY22 at 8.3-21.0x FY23's. Starting the window at the break (1-Apr-2022, FY23 being the first stepped-up year) and pairing it with the peers' move over the same window (+7.8%) gives **37x (₹16,120, -24% vs the price)**; starting in Apr-2023, once EPS had reached the FY24 level, gives 40.5x (₹17,640, -17%). **Neither changes the rating: all three windows give a SELL.** As in the Acutaas report, we keep the house window in the base and show the break windows as sensitivities.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a real CDMO step-up in a well-run chemistry company, priced as if the next one were certain; the rule says SELL

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a 40-year-old API maker with complex chemistry and a clean USFDA record that has turned itself into a contract manufacturer for innovators: CMS was 61% of FY26 revenue, EPS rose from ₹50 (FY22) to ₹284 (FY26), Q1FY27 revenue rose 119% and net cash was ₹309 cr at Jun-2026. **What you are not buying:** diversification (three customer groups were 54% of revenue; about three molecules drive CMS), predictable quarters, disclosure of those molecules, or a proven peptide business.

**What you are paying:** ₹21,350 is 55.0x trailing EPS, 52.7x our FY28E and 49.0x Sep-28E. On the street's method (P/E), Neuland's own 26.4x median since Apr-2021 lifted by the pharma sector's +8.2% gives 28.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹435.7 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a SELL under the house rule. The EV/EBITDA cross-check (₹12,411) agrees and the DCF (₹6,145) is lower still. Starting the window at the FY23 earnings break gives 37x (₹16,120), still a SELL; only the street's own multiple (Nuvama's 48x: ₹20,910) supports today's price. The latest broker targets (median ₹22,130) imply little upside too.

assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the four-line build below (checked in NEULANDLAB.ctx.js). Prime +10/8/7%: Q1FY27 Prime ~Rs116 cr (+23%), Ezetimibe 'likely to drive growth'; FY26 fell 5%. Specialty +8/12/12%: FY26 fell 16% on Paliperidone shipment delays at a customer; Q1FY27 ~Rs51 cr (+10%); Gland Pharma sterile collaboration and new DMFs (Vonoprazan, Edoxaban) later. Others grow with the business.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (before other income): 15.1% (FY22), 22.9% (FY23), 29.7% (FY24), 22.4% (FY25), 28.7% (FY26), 34.7% in Q1FY27 (Q4FY26 39.6%, Q1FY26 11.6%). FY27 31%: Q2-Q4 at ~29.7% vs 31.6% a year earlier. FY28-29 30.5%: the peptide plant and the new R&D centre add fixed costs before revenue, and FY26 had 'favourable conditions in terms of exchange rates'. dcf._tgWhy: 5.5%, mid-range of the house 5-6%; the company's own goodwill test uses 5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~15% (FY29E) to 7% by FY42E: revenue grew 15% a year in FY16-26 with long flat spells (FY18, FY22, FY25).

dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from 14-20% of sales (FY27-29E) to 7%: maintenance (~4.5% of sales, FY26 depreciation) plus growth capex at ~2.5x asset turnover.

Trough rule: no year is left out (FY23 Rs127.5 vs a Rs31.4 line, half of FY21's Rs62.9; FY25 Rs148.8 vs Rs116.9).
